citeAs: Zayene, M., Endres, J., Havolli, A., Corbiere, C., Cherkaoui, S., Kontouli, A., & Alahi, A. (2025). HELVIPAD: A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2411.18335v2.
creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbiere, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi (EPFL, TU Darmstadt)
description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions.
name: HELVIPAD
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy was assessed by calculating pixel error (Euclidean distances between 200 randomly selected LiDAR points and their image positions), resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels, and 8.0 pixels in visually challenging areas.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Accurate depth and disparity labels were created by projecting 3D LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images. Rotation and translation parameters were optimized by minimizing the error between projected points and their corresponding location on the equirectangular images.
rai:dataCollection: Collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a synchronized Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Given the sparse nature of LiDAR point clouds compared to high-resolution camera images, ground-truth depth labels cover only a fraction of the total pixels. A depth completion pipeline was developed to address this.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: 29 video sequences containing equirectangular images at 30 fps and LiDAR point clouds at 10 fps.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: A fully automated depth completion pipeline interpolates depth on spherical grid points by using temporally aggregated point clouds (4 preceding and 4 succeeding frames) and a weighted average of its k-nearest neighbors.
rai:dataLimitations: Occlusions were not explicitly handled. The depth completion approach is limited for fast-moving objects like cars and does not provide labels for pixels at object boundaries.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images and depth maps were cropped to remove unnecessary regions (sky, ground) and downsized from a width of 1024 pixels to 512, resulting in 39,553 paired images at a resolution of 1920x512 pixels.
rai:dataUseCases: Developing and benchmarking omnidirectional depth estimation models capable of navigating in human environments.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset captures human pedestrian activity, with an average of 13.33 pedestrians in indoor sequences and 17.65 pedestrians in outdoor sequences.
